name: MSPM0C1104SDSGR
title: MSPM0C110x / MSPS003 24 MHz Arm Cortex-M0+ mixed-signal microcontrollers, 8 or 16 KB flash, 1 KB SRAM
summary: A low-cost 32-bit microcontroller on a 24 MHz Arm Cortex-M0+ with 8 KB (MSPM0C1103, MSPS003F3) or 16 KB (MSPM0C1104, MSPS003F4) of flash and 1 KB of SRAM, running from 1.62 V to 3.6 V at -40 °C to 125 °C. It carries a 12-bit 1.5 Msps ADC with internal 1.4/2.5 V reference and temperature sensor, one advanced and two general-purpose 16-bit timers, a UART, an I2C and an SPI, a 1-channel DMA and an internal 24 MHz oscillator, so no crystal is needed. MSPM0C1104SDSGR is the 16 KB part in the 2 mm × 2 mm 8-pin WSON, with 6 GPIOs on tape and reel.
key_figures: 87 µA/MHz typ, 2.1 mA typ at 24 MHz, 3.3 V
609 µA typ at 4 MHz, 311 µA typ at 32 kHz
12-bit, 1.5 Msps (VDD reference), up to 10 external inputs
up to 18; 6 on 8-pin packages; two 5 V-tolerant open-drain

circuits.title: Typical application
circuits.description: Minimum connections around the chip, shown on the 8-pin DSG part. CVDD (10 µF low-ESR, the recommended bulk value) and a ceramic CDEC sit across VDD and VSS within a few millimetres of the pins. RpuNRST pulls NRST up to VDD with CNRST to ground, so the device leaves reset and another device or a debug probe can still drive NRST; the RC is optional but NRST must reach VDD. An open-drain pin (PA0 in this circuit) needs a pull-up Rpu to VDD or to a 5 V rail to drive high, since it has no high-side driver. SWDIO and SWCLK go to the debug tool.

parts.note: low-ESR, ±20% or tighter, at the VDD/VSS pins

notes: Values for CDEC, RpuNRST, CNRST and Rpu are given in TI's MSPM0 C-series hardware development guide.
The open-drain pins are fail-safe: they may carry a voltage while VDD is unpowered.

operation.text: MSPM0C1104 (16 KB flash) and MSPM0C1103 (8 KB flash) are 24 MHz Cortex-M0+ parts with 1 KB SRAM; MSPS003F4 and MSPS003F3 are the 16 KB and 8 KB parts in the 20-pin TSSOP. Packages are 20-pin VSSOP, TSSOP and WQFN, 16-pin SOT, and 8-pin SOT, WSON and DSBGA; the 8-pin parts bring out 6 GPIOs and 3 ADC inputs. All are rated -40 °C to 125 °C. Automotive versions MSPM0C1103-Q1 and MSPM0C1104-Q1 exist.

Arm Cortex-M0+ clocked from 32 kHz to 24 MHz, ARMv6-M Thumb (little endian), with a 32-cycle 32×32 multiply. The NVIC has 4 programmable priority levels and tail chaining. Flash runs with zero wait states up to 24 MHz.

Five modes, from highest to lowest power: RUN, SLEEP, STOP, STANDBY, SHUTDOWN, each with sub-policies (RUN0-2, SLEEP0-2, STOP0/2, STANDBY0/1). Peripheral interrupts wake the part from SLEEP, STOP and STANDBY; only NRST or SWD wake it from SHUTDOWN, where the core regulator is off and SRAM is lost. PD1 (CPU, memories, SPI0, CRC, DMA) is powered only in RUN and SLEEP; PD0 (timers, UART, I2C, GPIO, WWDT, ADC) stays powered through STANDBY. Both are off in SHUTDOWN.

The PMU makes the core supply and watches VDD with a power-on reset monitor and a brown-out monitor. BOR level 0 is the default; levels 1 to 3 can be chosen as early-warning thresholds. The PMU also holds the bandgap used by the analog blocks, and its trim is parity protected: a corrupted trim forces a POR at once. Start-up from VDD crossing VBOR0+ to the first instruction takes 210 µs typical.

Oscillators: SYSOSC (24 MHz, -2% to +1.2%) and LFOSC (32 kHz). External digital clock inputs: LFCLKIN (32 kHz) and HFCLKIN (4 to 24 MHz). Distributed clocks: MCLK for PD1 from SYSOSC or LFCLK (RUN, SLEEP); CPUCLK from MCLK (RUN); ULPCLK for PD0 (RUN to STANDBY); MFCLK, a fixed 4 MHz (RUN, SLEEP, STOP); LFCLK, a fixed 32 kHz (RUN to STANDBY); ADCCLK (RUN, SLEEP, STOP); CLK_OUT to a pin (RUN to STANDBY). No crystal is needed.

One DMA channel moves data without the CPU, for example ADC results into SRAM, so the CPU can stay asleep. Transfers of 8, 16, 32 or 64 bits or mixed, up to 64k transfers per block. Only the ADC can trigger it directly; other triggers come from software or the two generic subscribers.

An event fabric routes events from publishers to subscribers: to the CPU as interrupts, to the DMA as triggers, or straight to another peripheral (for example a timer starting ADC sampling). One generic 1:1 channel is available.
One flash bank with 1 KB sectors, programmable and erasable in circuit across the whole supply range. 100k erase/program cycles on 32 chosen sectors; 60 years retention at Tj ≤ 85 °C.

1 KB, zero wait states at all CPU clocks, kept in RUN, SLEEP, STOP and STANDBY and lost in SHUTDOWN. It can be write-protected in 1 KB steps, which guards code run from SRAM against stray CPU or DMA writes.

Up to 18 port A pins. Bits can be set, cleared or toggled without read-modify-write; inputs have user-set filtering. Each pin's PINCMx register sets its function, pull-up or pull-down, drive and speed, one digital function at a time. Two pins (PA0, PA1) are 5 V-tolerant open drain: low-side NMOS only, no pull-up, no high-side clamp, fail-safe when VDD is off. SDIO pins sink or source 6 mA; ODIO pins sink 20 mA.

12-bit SAR, single-ended, up to 1.5 Msps at 12 bits (1.7 Msps at 10 bits) with VDD as reference, and over 10 ENOB. Up to 10 external inputs plus internal channels for the temperature sensor (11), VREF (12) and a VDD/3 supply monitor (15). The reference is VDD or the internal 1.4 V or 2.5 V VREF. It runs in RUN, SLEEP and STOP and accepts triggers from STANDBY.

An on-chip sensor whose voltage falls about 1.9 mV/°C, read on ADC channel 11. Each unit stores one factory calibration code, taken in 12-bit mode with the 1.4 V VREF at the trim temperature (30 °C typical); with the coefficient TSc it gives the die temperature.
A buffered internal reference for the ADC, selectable 1.4 V (works from VDD 1.62 V) or 2.5 V (needs VDD ≥ 2.7 V). With it the ADC reaches 1 Msps at 10 bits.
Debug security, a unique die ID and flash write/erase protection. The CRC block computes CRC16-CCITT, with custom polynomial and bit reversal.

UART0 handles 5 to 8 data bits, even/odd/stick/no parity, 1 or 2 stop bits, line break, input glitch filtering and 16x, 8x or 3x oversampling, with 4-entry TX and RX FIFOs and loopback. It supports LIN, DALI, IrDA, ISO7816 smart card, Manchester, 9-bit mode and hardware flow control, and keeps working in STOP and STANDBY.

SPI0 works as controller or peripheral up to 12 Mbit/s (ULPCLK/2), with programmable prescaler, chip selects, 4-entry FIFOs, and frames of 4 to 16 bits as controller or 7 to 16 bits as peripheral. Formats: Motorola, TI and National Microwire.

I2C0 runs as controller or target at 100 kbit/s, 400 kbit/s and 1 Mbit/s (Fm+), with 7- and 10-bit addresses, several target addresses, clock stretching, 4-entry FIFOs, analog and digital glitch filters, SMBus 3.0 (PEC, ARP, timeouts) and PMBus. An address match wakes the part from STOP.

The windowed watchdog has a 25-bit counter, a clock divider, eight periods and eight window sizes; a missed service gives a reset or an interrupt. It can stop automatically in sleep modes or serve as a plain interval timer.

TIMG14 (four channels) and TIMG8 (two channels, quadrature encoder and Hall inputs) are 16-bit general-purpose timers with 8-bit prescalers. TIMA0 is a 16-bit advanced timer with four channels plus two internal ones, complementary outputs with dead band, an 8-bit repeat counter, shadow registers and fault inputs that force the outputs to a safe state. All three sit in PD0, can trigger each other and the ADC, and together give up to 14 PWM outputs. A beeper output gives 1, 2, 4 or 8 kHz square waves.

Two-wire SWD on PA19 (SWDIO, internal pull-up) and PA20 (SWCLK, internal pull-down), both enabled at reset and usable as GPIO when SWD is disabled. Debug works in every low-power mode, with run/halt/step, 2 hardware breakpoints and 1 watchpoint, peripheral halt control, a mailbox to the boot ROM, SWD lockout and password-protected debug. SWD runs to 10 MHz.

Put low-ESR ceramic decoupling across VDD and VSS within a few millimetres of the pins, with at least 10 µF bulk (larger bulk slows the supply ramp). NRST must be pulled to VDD for the device to boot; a pull-up with a capacitor to ground lets another device or a probe drive it. Open-drain pins need external pull-ups to drive high, to VDD or a 5 V rail. Unused PA pins are set as GPIO and driven low or given an internal pull.
The FACTORY region holds read-only DEVICEID and USERID words identifying the part and package, plus factory trims. The silicon revision also appears in the top-side marking.
